# CV-21 — Agents and MCP tools

> Branch `t/maciej/cv-21-agents-mcp` · head: see the hand-back · status: built, not landed
> Migration: `supabase/migrations/20261017000000_chat_v2_agents.sql` · applied to the local stack: yes, 2026-10-16, after CV-20 (live bodies re-read after CV-20 landed; none of the ones redefined here had changed)

## Delivered against the row

- **`chat_op_agent_post` as the creator** (same signature, so the deployed connector keeps working until the release redeploys it): `author_id` the key's creator, `author_kind 'api_key'`, `author_label` the key's name, `api_key_id` the key. The fourth argument is the message it answers (a v1 thread root reads as before); a reply joins that message's chain with the quote, like `chat_op_send` (locks, `reply_user_ids`, `chat__reopen_chain`); with no channel given, the answered message's conversation. Mentions read like a person's send (`chat__read_mentions`): `@channel` only if the creator may (else plain text); announcement channels only for a creator who manages them; the creator's role, removal and the plan cap it. References link "Mentioned in" as the creator (`chat__link_mentions`). It never moves the creator's read mark.
- **The key's rules, once:** `chat__key_actor(need)` returns the key's workspace, its creator and its switch, and refuses a missing scope, the plan, or a creator who no longer reads chat. `chat__key_reads_channel(channel, creator, private_ok)` covers channels only (never a direct message): public ones, and private ones only with the switch while the creator is a member. Every key read and write goes through them.
- **30 posts a minute per key:** `chat_send_limit`'s per-key branch now applies, because `api_key_id` is set (10 in 10 s too, like everyone).
- **`workspace_api_keys.include_private_chat boolean not null default false`**, set by `workspace_api_keys_set_private_chat(key, on)`. KEYS-1's scopes map, its normalizer and its CHECK are untouched. In the key editor it is a switch under the scopes ("Include private channels I'm in"), shown while the key reads chat, and saved at once.
- **`chat_my_keys(workspace)`**: your own live keys that read chat, whatever your role now (they still post as you), for Settings' reply switches. The column is granted to clients column by column, like the rest of the table.
- **`chat_key_readers(channel)`** lists the people whose live, chat-reading keys with the switch on read this private channel (themselves members). Details' People section ends with "An app of Alex's can read this" / "An app of yours …" / "Apps of …".
- **Reads for the connector, as the creator:** `chat_agent_conversations`, `chat_agent_messages` (a conversation's top-level messages or a chain; keyset pages, a page may start from a message id alone), `chat_agent_search` (chat_search's own query, shared through `chat__search_in`; `chat_search` itself still answers people only), and `chat_agent_addressed` (the creator's open Catch up mentions, team mentions, @channel, replies and announcements in conversations the key reads; never a direct message).
- **Writes for the connector, one body each:** `chat__react_as`, `chat__mark_decision_as`, `chat__wrap_up_as` and `chat__create_channel_as` take the acting person. `chat_op_react`, `_mark_decision`, `_wrap_up` and `_create_channel` pass `auth.uid()` (unchanged for the app). `chat_op_agent_react`, `_mark_decision`, `_wrap_up` and `_create_channel` pass the key's creator after the key's rules. Trails read "<person> · via <key>" (TV-D16's `module_activity_log`).
- **Fan-out:** while the key itself is acting (`module_api_key_id()` is the post's key), its post reaches its creator like anyone's (a mention, Every message: "counts as new"). A reply to a key's post brings its creator into the chain only while that key's notification switch is on (`user_preferences.preferences.chatKeyReplies.<key id>`, on when unset), unless the reply mentions them. Bell rows, notice titles and emails say "Alex · via CI key". When the creator edits a key's post in the app, the edit is theirs: they aren't told of it, and its trail is theirs.
- **Counts:** `chat_unread_counts` and `chat_catchup_open` count a key's posts as unread for their creator, and replies to them only through the switch. In the app, too: the "New" line, the new-messages pill, a chain's fresh count and the screen-reader announcement treat a key's post as new to you. ↑ in an empty composer still edits only what you wrote yourself.
- **The ten tools** (`modules/chat.ts`): `chat_list_channels`, `chat_read` (a conversation or a chain, `before` pages), `chat_search`, `chat_addressed_to_me` (View), and `chat_post`, `chat_reply`, `chat_react`, `chat_mark_decision`, `chat_wrap_up`, `chat_create_channel` (Edit). Each is one RPC, with no table read in the connector. Names are matched as typed. Their argument contracts are in `mcp-tool-args.ts`.
- **Manifest:** `chatModuleManifest` lists the five agent ops and four reads, in lockstep with the connector (a test checks it).
- **App:** "Alex Rivera · via Claude" with Alex's avatar and no badge (rows, search hits, export); v1 app posts keep "<key name>" + "app". Settings → Preferences → Chat gets one switch per key of yours that reads chat: "Replies to posts by <key>".

## Agent's choices (deferred to by Maciej: confirmed for building, may be reconsidered)

- **The post keeps its v1 signature** · the old connector calls `p_parent_id` by name, and renaming it would break the deployed connector between the migration and the redeploy · rejected: `p_reply_to_id` with DROP + CREATE.
- **A key's reply switch lives in the person's preferences** (`chatKeyReplies`, on by default), in Settings → Preferences → Chat · it's the creator's notification, and a column on the key would let any key manager change it · rejected: a column on `workspace_api_keys`; inside `notifications` (a map in a map of booleans).
- **Switch off = the reply doesn't reach the creator at all** (no Catch up item, bell or notice) unless it mentions them; switch on = an ordinary reply (the "Mentions and replies" switch still governs its notice) · "reach you only through that key's switch" · rejected: a held Catch up item (CV-18's pattern), which would still pile up CI chatter.
- **Only the key's creator turns "Include private channels I'm in" on; any key manager turns it off** · it opens the creator's own channels · rejected: any manager.
- **Announcement channels refuse the post** for a creator who doesn't manage them (an agent's `@channel` from a creator who may not is sent as plain text) · a post in an announcement channel can't be turned into plain text.
- **A key creates a private channel only with its switch on** · otherwise it couldn't read what it made. A key without private access checks name clashes against public channels only (the creator's private channels play no part).
- **The creator's own agent's replies are new to them, never a reply item** (orchestrator's call, revisitable): in a chain the creator is in, a reply posted through their own key gives them no Catch up "reply" item, bell row or device notice and doesn't count as addressed to them; it still counts as unread (and as an Every-message line on that level). Someone else's reply in that chain reaches them as usual. `chat_agent_addressed` never hands a key its own posts back · rejected: the agent's replies as ordinary replies (its creator would be told of their own agent's work).
- **A key's post is the creator's for edit, delete and wrap-up on the server** (the `author_id = you` rules) · the post is theirs, via a delegate · rejected: special-casing `author_kind` in four ops. The app offers Edit, ↑-edit and "Reply privately" only on what a person wrote.
- **The reply switch applies live to counts, and at the time of each reply to Catch up** · turning it on later counts earlier replies as addressed without a Catch up item behind them (turning it off hides them from the count at once) · rejected: re-reading stored items in the count (CV-5's live count rule).
- **A key's post that mentions its own creator keeps them in that chain** whatever the switch (the mention is explicit).
- **The agent ops take the workspace id** (react, decision, wrap up) and refuse another workspace's · every manifest op is workspace-scoped.
- **Details' line only for private channels** · a public channel is readable by every chat key, so naming them adds nothing.

## Gotchas (area: supabase)

- `chat__chain_root` reads `chat_can_read_channel` (auth.uid()): any body run for a key's creator needs a person-parameter twin (`chat__chain_root_as`). Check every helper an `_as` body calls.
- The connector rejects any tool without an arguments schema in `_shared/contracts/mcp-tool-args.ts` ("unknown tool"), and `z.object` strips unknown keys: a new tool argument must be added there too.
- The local edge runtime serves whichever worktree started the stack. To round-trip this worktree's connector, run a one-off `edge-runtime` container on `supabase_network_moduo` with `--main-service=<functions>/moduo-mcp` (it reads `deno.json` without `--import-map`), and pass `SUPABASE_URL=http://kong:8000` and `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEYS`.

## For later blocks

- **CV-23 / release:** redeploy `moduo-mcp` after the migration (the old connector's four tools keep working on the new post; its `chat_read`/`chat_search` read tables directly until then and see only public channels).
- **Later:** `chat__move_relink` still relinks people's messages only (`author_kind = 'user'`); a moved key post keeps no "Mentioned in" links.
- **Later:** `chat__fire_later` still counts only other people's messages as new when a Later item returns; a key's posts there are ignored.

## Manual checklist (step → expect → surface)

- [ ] Settings → API keys → Edit access on your key → set Chat to View → "Include private channels I'm in" appears, off → turn it on → toast; reload keeps it → web
- [ ] Someone else's key (as an admin) → the switch is disabled while off ("Only Alex can turn this on") → web
- [ ] Post through the key (MCP `chat_post`) → the message reads "You · via <key>" with your avatar, no "app" badge → web
- [ ] Teammate replies to it → it reaches you in Catch up and the bell; turn off Settings → Preferences → Chat → "Replies to posts by <key>"; the next reply doesn't; a reply that @mentions you does → web
- [ ] Private channel you're in, key with the switch on → Details → People ends with "An app of yours can read this" → web

## Notes

- `chat__sender_label` is left as is: for a post through a key it names "<person> · via <key>" in notices and emails, also when its creator later edits it.
- The `has_column_privilege(… include_private_chat …)` check in `chat_agents.test.sql` can't fail on the local stack (its table grants are broader than prod's column grants); it guards the grant against prod's dump.
- Client counts follow the server: the store counts a post through your own key as new (`countArrival`, mark-unread's recount), and a reply to your key's post is addressed to you only while `chatKeyReplies[key]` is on (`keyRepliesOn`, read from preferences); `apiKeyId` now rides the message columns.

## Verify before release

- Apply the migration, then redeploy `moduo-mcp` and run `scripts/mcp-roundtrip.ts --chat-write <channel>` with a View key and an Edit key on a test workspace.
- `agents_privacy.test.sql` fails 2 import checks on the local stack with or without this migration (local grant drift).
